requirements.name: Resource logs in Logic Apps should be enabled
requirements.description: Audit enabling of resource logs. This enables you to recreate activity trails to use for investigation purposes; when a security incident occurs or when your network is compromised.

requirements.name: Network Watcher should be enabled
requirements.description: Network Watcher is a regional service that enables you to monitor and diagnose conditions at a network scenario level in, to, and from Azure. Scenario level monitoring enables you to diagnose problems at an end to end network level view. It is required to have a network watcher resource group to be created in every region where a virtual network is present. An alert is enabled if a network watcher resource group is not available in a particular region.

requirements.name: Resource logs in Search services should be enabled
requirements.description: Audit enabling of resource logs. This enables you to recreate activity trails to use for investigation purposes; when a security incident occurs or when your network is compromised.

requirements.name: Auto provisioning of the Log Analytics agent should be enabled on your subscription
requirements.description: To monitor for security vulnerabilities and threats, Azure Security Center collects data from your Azure virtual machines. Data is collected by the Log Analytics agent, formerly known as the Microsoft Monitoring Agent (MMA), which reads various security-related configurations and event logs from the machine and copies the data to your Log Analytics workspace for analysis. We recommend enabling auto provisioning to automatically deploy the agent to all supported Azure VMs and any new ones that are created.

rejected_reasons: Monitoring agent auto-provisioning is retired and cannot be enabled.

requirements.name: Azure Defender for App Service should be enabled
requirements.description: Azure Defender for App Service leverages the scale of the cloud, and the visibility that Azure has as a cloud provider, to monitor for common web app attacks.

requirements.name: Microsoft Defender for Containers should be enabled
requirements.description: Microsoft Defender for Containers provides hardening, vulnerability assessment and run-time protections for your Azure, hybrid, and multi-cloud Kubernetes environments.

requirements.name: Ensure That Microsoft Defender for Databases is set to 'On'
requirements.description: Turning on Microsoft Defender for Databases enables threat detection for the instances running your database software. This provides threat intelligence, anomaly detection, and behavior analytics in the Azure Microsoft Defender for Cloud. Instead of being enabled on services like Platform as a Service (PaaS), this implementation will run within your instances as Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) on the Operating Systems hosting your databases.

requirements.name: Azure Defender for Key Vault should be enabled
requirements.description: Azure Defender for Key Vault provides an additional layer of protection and security intelligence by detecting unusual and potentially harmful attempts to access or exploit key vault accounts.

requirements.name: Azure Defender for Resource Manager should be enabled
requirements.description: Azure Defender for Resource Manager automatically monitors the resource management operations in your organization. Azure Defender detects threats and alerts you about suspicious activity.

requirements.name: Azure Defender for servers should be enabled
requirements.description: Azure Defender for servers provides real-time threat protection for server workloads and generates hardening recommendations as well as alerts about suspicious activities.

requirements.name: Azure Defender for Azure SQL Database servers should be enabled
requirements.description: Azure Defender for SQL provides functionality for surfacing and mitigating potential database vulnerabilities, detecting anomalous activities that could indicate threats to SQL databases, and discovering and classifying sensitive data.

requirements.name: Azure Defender for SQL should be enabled for unprotected SQL Managed Instances
requirements.description: Audit each SQL Managed Instance without advanced data security.

requirements.name: Microsoft Defender for Storage (Classic) should be enabled
requirements.description: Azure Defender for Storage provides detections of unusual and potentially harmful attempts to access or exploit storage accounts.

requirements.name: Resource logs in Service Bus should be enabled
requirements.description: Audit enabling of resource logs. This enables you to recreate activity trails to use for investigation purposes; when a security incident occurs or when your network is compromised.

requirements.name: Auditing on SQL server should be enabled
requirements.description: Auditing on your SQL Server should be enabled to track database activities across all databases on the server and save them in an audit log.

requirements.name: SQL servers with auditing to storage account destination should be configured with 90 days retention or higher
requirements.description: For incident investigation purposes, we recommend setting the data retention for your SQL Server' auditing to storage account destination to at least 90 days. Confirm that you are meeting the necessary retention rules for the regions in which you are operating. This is sometimes required for compliance with regulatory standards.

requirements.name: Azure Defender for SQL should be enabled for unprotected Azure SQL servers
requirements.description: Audit SQL servers without Advanced Data Security.

requirements.name: Resource logs in Azure Stream Analytics should be enabled
requirements.description: Audit enabling of resource logs. This enables you to recreate activity trails to use for investigation purposes; when a security incident occurs or when your network is compromised.

requirements.name: Function apps should have 'Client Certificates (Incoming client certificates)' enabled
requirements.description: Client certificates allow for the app to request a certificate for incoming requests. Only clients with valid certificates will be able to reach the app.

requirements.name: Function apps should not have CORS configured to allow every resource to access your apps
requirements.description: Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) should not allow all domains to access your Function app. Allow only required domains to interact with your Function app.

requirements.name: Ensure the web app has 'Client Certificates (Incoming client certificates)' set to 'On'
requirements.description: Client certificates allow for the app to request a certificate for incoming requests. Only clients that have a valid certificate will be able to reach the app.

requirements.name: Linux machines should meet requirements for the Azure compute security baseline
requirements.description: Requires that prerequisites are deployed to the policy assignment scope. Machines are non-compliant if the machine is not configured correctly for one of the recommendations in the Azure compute security baseline.

requirements.name: Windows machines should meet requirements of the Azure compute security baseline
requirements.description: Requires that prerequisites are deployed to the policy assignment scope. Machines are non-compliant if the machine is not configured correctly for one of the recommendations in the Azure compute security baseline.

requirements.name: Azure Policy Add-on for Kubernetes service (AKS) should be installed and enabled on your clusters
requirements.description: Azure Policy Add-on for Kubernetes service (AKS) extends Gatekeeper v3, an admission controller webhook for Open Policy Agent (OPA), to apply at-scale enforcements and safeguards on your clusters in a centralized, consistent manner.

requirements.name: Deploy the Windows Guest Configuration extension to enable Guest Configuration assignments on Windows VMs
requirements.description: This policy deploys the Windows Guest Configuration extension to Windows virtual machines hosted in Azure that are supported by Guest Configuration. The Windows Guest Configuration extension is a prerequisite for all Windows Guest Configuration assignments and must be deployed to machines before using any Windows Guest Configuration policy definition.

requirements.name: Audit Windows machines that do not store passwords using reversible encryption
requirements.description: Requires that prerequisites are deployed to the policy assignment scope. Machines are non-compliant if Windows machines that do not store passwords using reversible encryption.

requirements.name: Key Vault keys should have an expiration date
requirements.description: Cryptographic keys should have a defined expiration date and not be permanent. Keys that are valid forever provide a potential attacker with more time to compromise the key. It is a recommended security practice to set expiration dates on cryptographic keys.

requirements.name: Key Vault secrets should have an expiration date
requirements.description: Secrets should have a defined expiration date and not be permanent. Secrets that are valid forever provide a potential attacker with more time to compromise them. It is a recommended security practice to set expiration dates on secrets.

requirements.name: Audit Windows machines that do not restrict the minimum password length to 14 characters
requirements.description: Requires that prerequisites are deployed to the policy assignment scope. Machines are non-compliant if Windows machines that do not restrict the minimum password length to 14 characters.

requirements.name: Audit Windows machines that do not have the password complexity setting enabled
requirements.description: Requires that prerequisites are deployed to the policy assignment scope. Machines are non-compliant if Windows machines that do not have the password complexity setting enabled.

requirements.name: Audit Windows machines that allow re-use of the previous 24 passwords
requirements.description: Requires that prerequisites are deployed to the policy assignment scope. Machines are non-compliant if Windows machines that allow re-use of the previous 24 passwords.

requirements.name: Subscriptions should have a contact email address for security issues
requirements.description: To ensure the relevant people in your organization are notified when there is a potential security breach in one of your subscriptions, set a security contact to receive email notifications from Security Center.

requirements.name: Email notification for high severity alerts should be enabled
requirements.description: To ensure the relevant people in your organization are notified when there is a potential security breach in one of your subscriptions, enable email notifications for high severity alerts in Security Center.

requirements.name: Email notification to subscription owner for high severity alerts should be enabled
requirements.description: To ensure your subscription owners are notified when there is a potential security breach in their subscription, set email notifications to subscription owners for high severity alerts in Security Center.

requirements.name: Key vaults should have deletion protection enabled
requirements.description: Malicious deletion of a key vault can lead to permanent data loss. A malicious insider in your organization can potentially delete and purge key vaults. Purge protection protects you from insider attacks by enforcing a mandatory retention period for soft deleted key vaults. No one inside your organization or Microsoft will be able to purge your key vaults during the soft delete retention period.

requirements.name: Key vaults should have soft delete enabled
requirements.description: Deleting a key vault without soft delete enabled permanently deletes all secrets, keys, and certificates stored in the key vault. Accidental deletion of a key vault can lead to permanent data loss. Soft delete allows you to recover an accidentally deleted key vault for a configurable retention period.

requirements.name: Geo-redundant backup should be enabled for Azure Database for MariaDB
requirements.description: Azure Database for MariaDB allows you to choose the redundancy option for your database server. It can be set to a geo-redundant backup storage in which the data is not only stored within the region in which your server is hosted, but is also replicated to a paired region to provide recovery option in case of a region failure. Configuring geo-redundant storage for backup is only allowed during server create.

rejected_reasons: Rejected as obsolete: Azure Database for MariaDB was retired on 19 September 2025; servers can no longer be created or run, so the control has no live resource to evaluate.

requirements.name: Geo-redundant backup should be enabled for Azure Database for MySQL
requirements.description: Azure Database for MySQL allows you to choose the redundancy option for your database server. It can be set to a geo-redundant backup storage in which the data is not only stored within the region in which your server is hosted, but is also replicated to a paired region to provide recovery option in case of a region failure. Configuring geo-redundant storage for backup is only allowed during server create.

rejected_reasons: Rejected as obsolete: Azure Database for MySQL Single Server (Microsoft.DBforMySQL/servers) was retired on 16 September 2024; the equivalent flexible-server controls are ported separately.

requirements.description: Azure Database for PostgreSQL allows you to choose the redundancy option for your database server. rejected_reasons: Rejected as obsolete: Azure Database for PostgreSQL Single Server (Microsoft.DBforPostgreSQL/servers) was retired on 28 March 2025; flexible-server equivalents are ported separately.

requirements.name: A vulnerability assessment solution should be enabled on your virtual machines
requirements.description: Audits virtual machines to detect whether they are running a supported vulnerability assessment solution. A core component of every cyber risk and security program is the identification and analysis of vulnerabilities. Azure Security Center's standard pricing tier includes vulnerability scanning for your virtual machines at no extra cost. Additionally, Security Center can automatically deploy this tool for you.

rejected_reasons: Upstream requires both an MDE.Linux/MDE.Windows extension and the integrated Qualys agent (WindowsAgent/LinuxAgent.AzureSecurityCenter). The integrated Qualys scanner has been retired; Defender for Cloud now uses Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management with agentless scanning on by default, so extension inventory cannot show whether a VM is assessed.

requirements.name: Vulnerability assessment should be enabled on SQL Managed Instance
requirements.description: Audit each SQL Managed Instance which doesn't have recurring vulnerability assessment scans enabled. Vulnerability assessment can discover, track, and help you remediate potential database vulnerabilities.

requirements.name: SQL databases should have vulnerability findings resolved
requirements.description: Monitor vulnerability assessment scan results and recommendations for how to remediate database vulnerabilities.

requirements.name: Vulnerability assessment should be enabled on your SQL servers
requirements.description: Audit Azure SQL servers which do not have recurring vulnerability assessment scans enabled. Vulnerability assessment can discover, track, and help you remediate potential database vulnerabilities.

requirements.name: Vulnerability assessment should be enabled on your Synapse workspaces
requirements.description: Discover, track, and remediate potential vulnerabilities by configuring recurring SQL vulnerability assessment scans on your Synapse workspaces.

requirements.name: Web Application Firewall (WAF) should be enabled for Application Gateway
requirements.description: Deploy Azure Web Application Firewall (WAF) in front of public facing web applications for additional inspection of incoming traffic. Web Application Firewall (WAF) provides centralized protection of your web applications from common exploits and vulnerabilities such as SQL injections, Cross-Site Scripting, local and remote file executions. You can also restrict access to your web applications by countries, IP address ranges, and other http(s) parameters via custom rules.

requirements.name: Web Application Firewall (WAF) should be enabled for Azure Front Door Service

You can also restrict access to your web applications by countries, IP address ranges, and other http(s) parameters via custom rules.

requirements.name: App Service apps should use the latest TLS version
requirements.description: Periodically, newer versions are released for TLS either due to security flaws, include additional functionality, and enhance speed. Upgrade to the latest TLS version for App Service apps to take advantage of security fixes, if any, and/or new functionalities of the latest version.

requirements.name: FTPS only should be required in your Function App
requirements.description: Enable FTPS enforcement for enhanced security.

requirements.name: Function apps should use the latest TLS version
requirements.description: Periodically, newer versions are released for TLS either due to security flaws, include additional functionality, and enhance speed. Upgrade to the latest TLS version for Function apps to take advantage of security fixes, if any, and/or new functionalities of the latest version.

requirements.name: Function apps should only be accessible over HTTPS
requirements.description: Use of HTTPS ensures server/service authentication and protects data in transit from network layer eavesdropping attacks.

requirements.name: FTPS should be required in your Web App
requirements.description: Enable FTPS enforcement for enhanced security.

requirements.name: Web Application should only be accessible over HTTPS
requirements.description: Use of HTTPS ensures server/service authentication and protects data in transit from network layer eavesdropping attacks.

requirements.name: Azure HDInsight clusters should use encryption in transit to encrypt communication between Azure HDInsight cluster nodes
requirements.description: Data can be tampered with during transmission between Azure HDInsight cluster nodes. Enabling encryption in transit addresses problems of misuse and tampering during this transmission.

requirements.name: Enforce SSL connection should be enabled for MySQL database servers
requirements.description: Azure Database for MySQL supports connecting your Azure Database for MySQL server to client applications using Secure Sockets Layer (SSL). Enforcing SSL connections between your database server and your client applications helps protect against 'man in the middle' attacks by encrypting the data stream between the server and your application. This configuration enforces that SSL is always enabled for accessing your database server.

requirements.name: Only secure connections to your Azure Cache for Redis should be enabled

Use of secure connections ensures authentication between the server and the service and protects data in transit from network layer attacks such as man-in-the-middle, eavesdropping, and session-hijacking.

requirements.name: Secure transfer to storage accounts should be enabled
requirements.description: Audit requirement of Secure transfer in your storage account. Secure transfer is an option that forces your storage account to accept requests only from secure connections (HTTPS). Use of HTTPS ensures authentication between the server and the service and protects data in transit from network layer attacks such as man-in-the-middle, eavesdropping, and session-hijacking.

requirements.name: Azure Batch account should use customer-managed keys to encrypt data
requirements.description: Use customer-managed keys to manage the encryption at rest of your Batch account's data. By default, customer data is encrypted with service-managed keys, but customer-managed keys are commonly required to meet regulatory compliance standards. Customer-managed keys enable the data to be encrypted with an Azure Key Vault key created and owned by you. You have full control and responsibility for the key lifecycle, including rotation and management.

requirements.name: Cognitive Services accounts should enable data encryption with a customer-managed key
requirements.description: Customer-managed keys are commonly required to meet regulatory compliance standards. Customer-managed keys enable the data stored in Cognitive Services to be encrypted with an Azure Key Vault key created and owned by you. You have full control and responsibility for the key lifecycle, including rotation and management.

requirements.name: OS and data disks should be encrypted with a customer-managed key
requirements.description: Use customer-managed keys to manage the encryption at rest of the contents of your managed disks. By default, the data is encrypted at rest with platform-managed keys, but customer-managed keys are commonly required to meet regulatory compliance standards. Customer-managed keys enable the data to be encrypted with an Azure Key Vault key created and owned by you. You have full control and responsibility for the key lifecycle, including rotation and management. Learn more at https://aka.ms/disks-cmk.

requirements.name: Managed disks should be double encrypted with both platform-managed and customer-managed keys
requirements.description: High security sensitive customers who are concerned of the risk associated with any particular encryption algorithm, implementation, or key being compromised can opt for additional layer of encryption using a different encryption algorithm/mode at the infrastructure layer using platform managed encryption keys. The disk encryption sets are required to use double encryption.

requirements.name: Container Instance container group should use customer-managed key for encryption
requirements.description: Secure your containers with greater flexibility using customer-managed keys. When you specify a customer-managed key, that key is used to protect and control access to the key that encrypts your data. Using customer-managed keys provides additional capabilities to control rotation of the key encryption key or cryptographically erase data.

requirements.name: Automation account variables should be encrypted

OS/data disk caches are encrypted at rest with either customer-managed or platform-managed key, depending on the encryption type selected on the disk.

requirements.name: Azure Stack Edge devices should use double-encryption
requirements.description: To secure the data at rest on the device, ensure it's double-encrypted, the access to data is controlled, and once the device is deactivated, the data is securely erased off the data disks. Double encryption is the use of two layers of encryption: BitLocker XTS-AES 256-bit encryption on the data volumes and built-in encryption of the hard drives. Learn more in the security overview documentation for the specific Stack Edge device.

requirements.name: Infrastructure encryption should be enabled for Azure Database for MySQL servers

Linking your component to a Log Analytics workspace that's enabled with a customer-managed key, ensures that your Application Insights logs meet this compliance requirement, see https://docs.microsoft.com/azure/azure-monitor/platform/customer-managed-keys.

requirements.name: Log Analytics agent should be installed on your virtual machine for Azure Security Center monitoring
requirements.description: This policy audits any Windows/Linux virtual machines if the Log Analytics extension is not installed.

rejected_reasons: Requires the Microsoft.EnterpriseCloud.Monitoring MicrosoftMonitoringAgent/OmsAgentForLinux extension. The Log Analytics agent is deprecated as of 31 August 2024 and unsupported; a PASS would reward an unsupported agent and a FAIL would flag VMs correctly migrated to Azure Monitor Agent.

requirements.name: Network traffic data collection agent should be installed on Linux virtual machines
requirements.description: Security Center uses the Microsoft Dependency agent to collect network traffic data from your Azure virtual machines to enable advanced network protection features such as traffic visualization on the network map, network hardening recommendations and specific network threats.

requirements.name: Network traffic data collection agent should be installed on Windows virtual machines
requirements.description: Security Center uses the Microsoft Dependency agent to collect network traffic data from your Azure virtual machines to enable advanced network protection features such as traffic visualization on the network map, network hardening recommendations and specific network threats.

requirements.name: Log Analytics workspaces should block log ingestion and querying from public networks
requirements.description: Improve workspace security by blocking log ingestion and querying from public networks. Only private-link connected networks will be able to ingest and query logs on this workspace. Learn more at https://aka.ms/AzMonPrivateLink#configure-log-analytics.

requirements.name: Log Analytics Workspaces should block non-Azure Active Directory based ingestion
requirements.description: Enforcing log ingestion to require Azure Active Directory authentication prevents unauthenticated logs from an attacker which could lead to incorrect status, false alerts, and incorrect logs stored in the system.

requirements.description: Traffic analytics analyzes flow logs to provide insights into traffic flow in your Azure cloud. requirements.name: Auto provisioning of the Log Analytics agent should be enabled on your subscription
requirements.description: To monitor for security vulnerabilities and threats, Azure Security Center collects data from your Azure virtual machines. Data is collected by the Log Analytics agent, formerly known as the Microsoft Monitoring Agent (MMA), which reads various security-related configurations and event logs from the machine and copies the data to your Log Analytics workspace for analysis. We recommend enabling auto provisioning to automatically deploy the agent to all supported Azure VMs and any new ones that are created.

requirements.name: SQL servers with auditing to storage account destination should be configured with 90 days retention or higher
requirements.description: For incident investigation purposes, we recommend setting the data retention for your SQL Server' auditing to storage account destination to at least 90 days. Confirm that you are meeting the necessary retention rules for the regions in which you are operating. This is sometimes required for compliance with regulatory standards.

requirements.name: App Configuration encryption should be enabled
requirements.description: Enabling App Configuration encryption helps protect and safeguard your data to meet your organizational security and compliance commitments.

requirements.name: App Service Environment should enable internal encryption
requirements.description: Setting InternalEncryption to true encrypts the pagefile, worker disks, and internal network traffic between the front ends and workers in an App Service Environment.

requirements.name: App Service apps should use the latest TLS version
requirements.description: Periodically, newer versions are released for TLS either due to security flaws, include additional functionality, and enhance speed. Upgrade to the latest TLS version for App Service apps to take advantage of security fixes, if any, and/or new functionalities of the latest version.

requirements.name: App Service API apps should only be accessible over HTTPS
requirements.description: Use of HTTPS ensures server/service authentication and protects data in transit from network layer eavesdropping attacks.

requirements.name: Function apps should use the latest TLS version

Upgrade to the latest TLS version for Function apps to take advantage of security fixes, if any, and/or new functionalities of the latest version.

requirements.name: Function apps should only be accessible over HTTPS
requirements.description: Use of HTTPS ensures server/service authentication and protects data in transit from network layer eavesdropping attacks.

requirements.name: Automation account variables should be encrypted
requirements.description: It is important to enable encryption of Automation account variable assets when storing sensitive data

requirements.name: Azure Key Vault should have firewall enabled
requirements.description: Enable the key vault firewall so that the key vault is not accessible by default to any public IPs. Optionally, you can configure specific IP ranges to limit access to those networks.

requirements.name: Key vaults should have deletion protection enabled
requirements.description: Malicious deletion of a key vault can lead to permanent data loss. A malicious insider in your organization can potentially delete and purge key vaults. Purge protection protects you from insider attacks by enforcing a mandatory retention period for soft deleted key vaults. No one inside your organization or Microsoft will be able to purge your key vaults during the soft delete retention period.

requirements.name: Key Vault secrets should have an expiration date
requirements.description: Secrets should have a defined expiration date and not be permanent. Secrets that are valid forever provide a potential attacker with more time to compromise them. It is a recommended security practice to set expiration dates on secrets.

requirements.name: Key vaults should have soft delete enabled
requirements.description: Deleting a key vault without soft delete enabled permanently deletes all secrets, keys, and certificates stored in the key vault. Accidental deletion of a key vault can lead to permanent data loss. Soft delete allows you to recover an accidentally deleted key vault for a configurable retention period.

requirements.name: Azure Key Vaults should use private link
requirements.description: Azure Private Link lets you connect your virtual networks to Azure services without a public IP address at the source or destination. The Private Link platform handles the connectivity between the consumer and services over the Azure backbone network. By mapping private endpoints to key vault, you can reduce data leakage risks.

requirements.name: Disk encryption should be enabled on Azure Data Explorer
requirements.description: Enabling disk encryption helps protect and safeguard your data to meet your organizational security and compliance commitments.

requirements.name: MySQL servers should use customer-managed keys to encrypt data at rest
requirements.description: Use customer-managed keys to manage the encryption at rest of your MySQL servers. By default, the data is encrypted at rest with service-managed keys, but customer-managed keys are commonly required to meet regulatory compliance standards. Customer-managed keys enable the data to be encrypted with an Azure Key Vault key created and owned by you. You have full control and responsibility for the key lifecycle, including rotation and management.

requirements.name: Infrastructure encryption should be enabled for Azure Database for MySQL servers
requirements.description: Enable infrastructure encryption for Azure Database for MySQL servers to have higher level of assurance that the data is secure. When infrastructure encryption is enabled, the data at rest is encrypted twice using FIPS 140-2 compliant Microsoft managed keys.

rejected_reasons: Rejected as obsolete: Azure Database for MySQL Single Server (Microsoft.DBforMySQL/servers) was retired on 16 September 2024; the equivalent flexible-server controls are ported separately.

requirements.name: Enforce SSL connection should be enabled for MySQL database servers
requirements.description: Azure Database for MySQL supports connecting your Azure Database for MySQL server to client applications using Secure Sockets Layer (SSL). Enforcing SSL connections between your database server and your client applications helps protect against 'man in the middle' attacks by encrypting the data stream between the server and your application. This configuration enforces that SSL is always enabled for accessing your database server.

requirements.name: Storage accounts should use customer-managed key for encryption
requirements.description: Secure your storage account with greater flexibility using customer-managed keys. When you specify a customer-managed key, that key is used to protect and control access to the key that encrypts your data. Using customer-managed keys provides additional capabilities to control rotation of the key encryption key or cryptographically erase data.

requirements.name: Storage account encryption scopes should use customer-managed keys to encrypt data at rest
requirements.description: Use customer-managed keys to manage the encryption at rest of your storage account encryption scopes. Customer-managed keys enable the data to be encrypted with an Azure key-vault key created and owned by you. You have full control and responsibility for the key lifecycle, including rotation and management.

requirements.name: Storage accounts should have infrastructure encryption
requirements.description: Enable infrastructure encryption for higher level of assurance that the data is secure. When infrastructure encryption is enabled, data in a storage account is encrypted twice.

requirements.name: Secure transfer to storage accounts should be enabled
requirements.description: Audit requirement of Secure transfer in your storage account. Secure transfer is an option that forces your storage account to accept requests only from secure connections (HTTPS). Use of HTTPS ensures authentication between the server and the service and protects data in transit from network layer attacks such as man-in-the-middle, eavesdropping, and session-hijacking.

requirements.name: Vulnerability assessment should be enabled on your Synapse workspaces
requirements.description: Discover, track, and remediate potential vulnerabilities by configuring recurring SQL vulnerability assessment scans on your Synapse workspaces.

requirements.name: App Service apps should have 'Client Certificates (Incoming client certificates)' enabled
requirements.description: Client certificates allow for the app to request a certificate for incoming requests. Only clients that have a valid certificate will be able to reach the app.
